name: UI interaction motion
controls: Which user interactions and system responses are animated inside the interface, and the exact motion treatment of each (cursor, input, controls, feedback, overlays, navigation, AI and data).
question: Which interactions should we see happen in the interface?
notes: These are the micro-interactions of a product film. In a video nobody is really clicking, so every interaction is choreographed: the cursor or finger must arrive before the target reacts, and the target must react within 60-120 ms or causality breaks. Keep interaction timing close to real product timing (feedback under 100 ms, small transitions 150-300 ms, overlays 200-400 ms) but slow the approach of the cursor enough to be followed. Pick the interactions the story needs; motion-language defines overall easing personality, ui-treatment defines what the UI looks like. Terms follow common UI-component naming (Material, Apple HIG, web component libraries); 'toast' vs 'snackbar' and 'drawer' vs 'sheet' vary by platform.

options.what: The on-screen mouse cursor travelling between targets as the viewer's proxy.
options.looks: A standard arrow cursor (often enlarged 1.5-2x for video), sometimes with a soft shadow or highlight halo.
options.motion: Curved, eased paths (not straight linear lines), accelerating out and decelerating into the target with a tiny settle; pauses 150-300 ms before acting.
options.use: Any cursor-driven demo, walkthroughs, desktop and web products.
options.conveys: A human is using this; it guides the eye to what matters.
options.vs: Pointer covers the style and state of the pointer (arrow, hand, I-beam, custom); cursor movement is the path and timing.
options.prompt: Animate the cursor on gently curved paths (arc offset 5-15% of distance) with power2.inOut, 500-900 ms per move depending on distance; overshoot by 0-3px and settle, pause 150-300 ms on the target before acting; scale the cursor 1.5-2x for legibility with a subtle 0 2px 6px shadow.

options.what: The pointer's shape and state changes: arrow, hand, I-beam, grab, resize, or a custom branded cursor.
options.looks: Arrow switches to a hand over links, I-beam over text, grab/grabbing hands during drag; custom cursors may be circles or labeled pills.
options.motion: Instant or 80-120 ms crossfade/morph between shapes as the pointer enters a target; custom circular cursors scale and blend over targets.
options.use: Detailed demos, design-tool marketing, websites with custom cursors.
options.conveys: Precision and affordance: the viewer knows what can be clicked or dragged.
options.vs: Cursor movement is the path; pointer states are the shape changes. Multiplayer cursors are other users' pointers with name labels.
options.prompt: Change the pointer shape on context: arrow to pointing hand over clickable targets, I-beam over text fields, open hand then closed hand during drag; morph between shapes in 80-120 ms; for a custom cursor, use a 16-24px circle that scales to 48px and inverts (mix-blend-mode: difference) over targets.

options.what: The moment the cursor or finger activates a target.
options.looks: Cursor dip, a press state on the target (darker fill, slight scale down), often a ripple or ring from the click point.
options.motion: Cursor scales to 0.9 for ~100 ms and returns; the target scales to 0.97 and darkens 6-10% within 60-120 ms; a ring expands from the click point to 24-40px and fades over 300-400 ms.
options.use: Every cursor-driven demo; the key cause-and-effect beat.
options.vs: Long press holds for a second action; hover is pre-click. A tap on mobile uses a finger-circle indicator instead of a cursor dip.
options.prompt: On click, scale the cursor to 0.9 for 100 ms then back; within 60-120 ms scale the target to 0.97 and darken its fill 8%, releasing over 150 ms; emit a 2px ring from the click point expanding from 0 to 32px while fading from 40% to 0 over 350 ms; the consequence (new state) starts 100-200 ms after the press.

options.what: The target's response when the pointer rests over it before clicking.
options.looks: Background tint, border brighten, slight lift or scale, revealed secondary actions, tooltip after a delay.
options.motion: 120-200 ms ease-out in, 150-250 ms ease-in out; lifts of 1-2px or scale 1.02; secondary actions fade and slide 4px.
options.use: Desktop and web demos, showing affordance and hidden actions.
options.conveys: Responsiveness and polish; the UI anticipates the user.
options.vs: Focus is keyboard-driven and shows a ring; hover is pointer-driven and subtle. Tooltip is a surface that may follow a hover.
options.prompt: When the cursor enters a target, over 150 ms ease-out lighten its background 4-6%, brighten the border to 20% contrast, and lift it 2px with a slightly larger shadow; reveal any hidden secondary actions with a 4px slide and fade; reverse over 200 ms when the cursor leaves.

options.what: The visual indicator that an element is active for keyboard input.
options.looks: A 2px accent ring offset 2px outside the element, or a glowing border on inputs; label may shift up.
options.motion: Ring expands from the element edge (spread 0 to 3px) over 120-160 ms; moves between fields in tab order; floating labels shrink and rise 150 ms.
options.use: Forms, keyboard-first products, accessibility-minded demos.
options.vs: Hover is transient pointer feedback; focus persists until another element takes it.
options.prompt: Show focus with a 2px accent ring offset 2px (box-shadow 0 0 0 2px bg, 0 0 0 4px accent) expanding from spread 0 over 140 ms ease-out; when an input focuses, raise its floating label to 75% size above the field in 150 ms; move focus to the next field by fading the old ring out as the new one grows in.

options.what: Text appearing in a field character by character as if typed.
options.looks: A caret advancing through the text, input grows or scrolls as needed.
options.motion: 30-60 ms per character with slight random variance (plus or minus 15 ms), short pauses at spaces and punctuation, caret solid while typing and blinking (530 ms) when idle.
options.use: Search, prompts, forms, AI input, code.
options.conveys: Human input and the moment of intent.
options.vs: Streaming text is system output arriving in tokens; typing is user input. Keyboard input shows the keys themselves.
options.prompt: Type text into the field at 35-55 ms per character with +/-15 ms random jitter, pausing 80-150 ms after spaces and 200-300 ms after punctuation; keep a 2px caret solid while typing and blink at 530 ms when idle; for long phrases compress the middle rather than speeding every key.

options.what: Showing physical key presses or shortcuts as part of the interaction.
options.looks: Keycap graphics (e.g. Cmd + K) appearing on screen, or a rendered keyboard with keys depressing.
options.motion: Keycaps press down 2-3px with a shadow collapse in 60-80 ms and release in 100 ms; combos press in sequence 80-120 ms apart and hold together.
options.use: Keyboard-first tools, shortcuts, developer products, power-user features.
options.conveys: Speed and mastery: no mouse needed.
options.vs: Typing shows text in a field; keyboard input shows the keys. Keystroke overlay is a specific persistent HUD of keys pressed.
options.prompt: Show pressed keys as keycap graphics (rounded 8px squares, 1px border, 3px bottom shadow edge, monospace or system-symbol glyph); press each key by translating it down 3px and collapsing the bottom shadow in 70 ms, release in 100 ms; for combos press modifiers first, 100 ms apart, then trigger the UI response on the final key.

options.what: A persistent on-screen display of keys being pressed, like screencast key visualizers.
options.looks: A pill or row of keycaps near the bottom center of the frame showing the current shortcut.
options.motion: Keys pop in (scale 0.9 to 1, 120 ms) as pressed, hold 600-900 ms, fade out 200 ms; new combos replace old ones with a quick crossfade.
options.use: Tutorials, developer tool demos, keyboard-driven workflows.
options.conveys: Transparency and teachability: you can do this too.
options.vs: Keyboard input animates a keyboard or keycaps as part of the scene; keystroke overlay is an instructional HUD layered above the demo.
options.prompt: Display pressed shortcuts in a dark translucent pill (rgba(0,0,0,0.7), 12px radius, 16px padding) centered 8% above the bottom edge; each keycap pops in with scale 0.9 to 1 over 120 ms, the combo holds 700 ms after the last press, then fades out over 200 ms.

options.what: Picking up an element and moving it with the pointer.
options.looks: Element lifts (larger shadow, slight scale, tilt), a placeholder or gap remains at the origin, neighbours shuffle.
options.motion: Lift in 120-160 ms (scale 1.03, shadow grows, rotate 1-3 degrees); element follows the cursor with slight lag (10-40 ms); other items part with 200 ms ease.
options.use: Kanban boards, reordering lists, builders, file management.
options.vs: Drop is the landing; drag is the pick-up and carry. Swipe is a quick flick gesture, not a carry.
options.prompt: On grab, switch the pointer to a closed hand, scale the item to 1.03, rotate it 2 degrees and increase its shadow to 0 16px 32px rgba(0,0,0,0.18) over 140 ms; follow the cursor with 20-30 ms of lag; leave a dashed 1px placeholder at the origin and slide neighbouring items apart over 200 ms power2.out.

options.what: An element landing in its new position or a drop zone accepting it.
options.looks: Drop zone highlights (dashed border becomes solid accent, tint) as the item approaches; item settles into place.
options.motion: Zone brightens on enter (150 ms); on release the item snaps into its slot with a quick settle (250-350 ms, slight overshoot or back.out(1.2)), shadow and tilt return to rest.
options.use: File uploads, kanban, builders, organising content.
options.conveys: Completion and order; the item belongs there.
options.vs: Drag is the carry; drop is the arrival and acceptance. Upload often starts with a drop.
options.prompt: When the dragged item enters the target, change the drop zone's 1.5px dashed border to solid accent and tint its fill to 8% accent over 150 ms; on release, snap the item into its slot with a 300 ms back.out(1.2), returning scale to 1, rotation to 0 and shadow to rest; flash the zone once then clear it.

options.what: Dragging a selection rectangle to select multiple items.
options.looks: A thin accent-bordered rectangle with 8-12% tinted fill growing from the drag start; selected items gain outlines or checkmarks.
options.motion: Rectangle grows with the cursor; each item gains its selected state the instant the box touches it (60-100 ms); on release the box fades in 150 ms.
options.use: Design tools, file managers, canvases, bulk actions.
options.conveys: Power and efficiency: act on many at once.
options.vs: Checkbox selects items one at a time; marquee selection selects spatially in one gesture.
options.prompt: Drag a selection rectangle from an empty point: 1px accent border, 10% accent fill, growing with the cursor over 400-700 ms; as each item intersects it, give the item a 1.5px accent outline in 80 ms; on release fade the rectangle out over 150 ms and show a bulk-action bar sliding up 12px.

options.what: Dragging an edge or handle to change a panel's or object's size.
options.looks: Resize cursor, visible handles or a highlighted edge, dimension readout; content reflows.
options.motion: Edge follows the cursor directly; contents reflow with 150-250 ms layout transitions; a size label updates live.
options.use: Design tools, window management, dashboards, split panes.
options.vs: Card expansion is a click-triggered size change; resize is a continuous user-driven drag.
options.prompt: Show 8px square handles or a highlighted 2px edge; drag it with a resize cursor over 600-900 ms; contents reflow via FLIP-style layout transitions (200 ms power2.out) and a small monospace size label (e.g. '640 x 420') updates live near the handle.

options.what: Other collaborators' cursors, each with a colored name label, moving in the same document.
options.looks: Colored arrow cursors with pill labels bearing names; avatars stacked in the header; selection outlines in each user's color.
options.motion: Cursors glide independently with slight smoothing (they update from the network, so movement is soft), labels trail the cursor; selections appear in each user's color.
options.use: Collaboration tools, design tools, docs, whiteboards.
options.vs: Cursor movement is the viewer's single guide; multiplayer cursors represent several people at once and must not compete with the main action.
options.prompt: Add 2-4 collaborator cursors, each a distinct saturated color with a pill name label (11-12px, same color fill, white text) attached bottom-right; move them on independent smooth paths (sine.inOut, 1-2 s moves with idle drift), and show their selections as outlines in their color; keep them smaller and quieter than the main cursor.

options.what: Content moving vertically within a view or page.
options.looks: Content sliding up behind fixed headers; a thin scrollbar indicator may appear; sticky elements pin.
options.motion: Eased momentum scrolling (power2.inOut or inertial deceleration), 400-1200 px per scroll beat, never linear; sticky headers pin and shrink; reveal-on-scroll elements animate as they enter.
options.use: Website tours, feeds, long documents, landing-page demos.
options.vs: Horizontal scroll moves sideways through carousels; page navigation replaces the view instead of moving through it.
options.prompt: Scroll content in discrete eased beats: 500-1000 px per beat over 700-1100 ms with power3.inOut, holding 600-1200 ms between beats so the content can be read; pin sticky headers and shrink them from 72px to 56px; show a 4px scrollbar thumb that fades in during movement and out 500 ms after.

options.what: Content moving sideways through a carousel, timeline or horizontal list.
options.looks: Row of cards partially cropped at the edge (implying more), pagination dots or arrows.
options.motion: Cards slide with momentum and snap to positions (scroll-snap feel), 300-500 ms power3.out; parallax between card image and card frame optional.
options.use: Galleries, templates, app store screenshots, timelines, feature carousels.
options.vs: Swipe is the gesture that may trigger it; horizontal scroll is the content motion. Tab switching changes views, not position in a row.
options.prompt: Show a row of cards with the last card cropped by the frame edge; move the row one card width at a time with 400 ms power3.out and a snap settle, updating pagination dots (active dot widens from 6px to 18px); optionally shift card imagery 20-30% slower than the card frames for parallax.

options.what: A quick directional finger gesture on a touch screen.
options.looks: A translucent finger-touch indicator (circle) that travels and fades, content following in the swipe direction.
options.motion: Touch circle appears (scale 0.8 to 1, 80 ms), travels 150-300px fast (200-300 ms), fades; content follows with the gesture then continues with momentum and snaps.
options.use: Mobile demos, card stacks (swipe to dismiss), photo browsing, onboarding.
options.vs: Drag is a slow carry; swipe is a fast flick that triggers momentum. Horizontal scroll is the content result.
options.prompt: Show touch with a 44px translucent white circle (30% opacity, 1px white border) appearing with scale 0.8 to 1 in 80 ms, travelling 200-300px in 220 ms with power2.out, then fading over 120 ms; content tracks the finger and continues with momentum to snap 300 ms later.

options.what: Two-finger gesture that scales content on a touch screen or trackpad.
options.looks: Two touch indicators moving apart or together, content scaling around their midpoint.
options.motion: Indicators diverge or converge over 400-700 ms; content scales around the midpoint in sync, then settles with a slight rubber-band if it exceeds limits.
options.use: Maps, photo apps, canvases, mobile demos.
options.vs: Zoom is the camera or content scale result (can happen without gesture); pinch is the gesture.
options.prompt: Show two 40px touch circles starting 60px apart, spreading to 220px over 500 ms power2.inOut; scale content around their midpoint in sync (e.g. 1 to 2.2x), then rubber-band 3% past the limit and settle back over 200 ms.

options.what: Scaling into or out of content, either in-product zoom or a virtual camera push on the UI.
options.looks: Content magnifies toward a focal region; detail sharpens; surrounding UI crops away.
options.motion: Smooth scale 1 to 1.5-3x over 600-1200 ms with power3.inOut, anchored on the region of interest; zoom out mirrors it.
options.use: Directing attention in demos, maps, canvases, detail reveals.
options.vs: Pinch is the touch gesture; zoom is the scale result. The camera dimension governs zooms of the whole composition; this is zoom inside the interface.
options.prompt: Zoom into the region of interest by scaling the interface 1 to 2x around that region's center over 900 ms power3.inOut; keep the target centered and sharp (render vectors at final resolution), hold, and zoom out with the same curve.

options.what: Holding a finger or button down to trigger a secondary action or menu.
options.looks: A progress ring or darkening that builds under the finger; the item lifts and the background blurs; a context menu or preview appears.
options.motion: Item slowly scales down to 0.95 over 400-600 ms (charging), then pops to 1.05 as the preview or menu opens with the background blurring.
options.use: Mobile app demos, hidden actions, previews.
options.vs: Click is instantaneous; long press has a visible charge-up. Context menu is often the result.
options.prompt: Hold the touch indicator on the item: scale the item from 1 to 0.95 over 500 ms linear-ish (power1.in) while a 2px ring fills around the touch point; then pop the item to 1.05 with back.out(1.6) over 250 ms, blur the background 12px and dim it 30%, and open the menu or preview beneath.

options.what: A thumb dragged along a track to set a continuous value.
options.looks: Track with filled portion in accent, round thumb, value label or tooltip above the thumb.
options.motion: Thumb grows 1.2x on grab; fill follows the thumb; value label counts in real time; a linked preview (image, chart, price) updates continuously.
options.use: Settings, pricing calculators, editing tools, filters.
options.vs: Toggle is binary; slider is continuous. Progress bar looks similar but is system-driven.
options.prompt: On grab, scale the thumb 1.2x in 100 ms and show a value bubble above it; drag it over 600-1000 ms with power2.inOut, filling the track in accent behind it, counting the value label in real time, and updating the linked preview continuously; on release shrink the thumb back in 150 ms.

options.what: A binary on/off switch.
options.looks: Pill track with a circular knob; track color changes from gray to accent when on.
options.motion: Knob slides across in 180-250 ms with a smooth ease (optionally stretching to a wider pill mid-travel), track color crossfades; the linked setting takes effect immediately.
options.use: Settings, feature flags, dark-mode demos, before/after reveals.
options.conveys: Instant control: flip a switch and it changes.
options.vs: Checkbox is for selection in lists or forms; a toggle takes effect immediately.
options.prompt: Animate the toggle knob across its pill track in 220 ms power2.inOut, stretching the knob width 1.3x at mid-travel and returning to round; crossfade the track from gray (#D1D5DB) to accent over the same duration; start the linked change (theme, feature) within 50 ms of the knob landing.

options.what: A square control checked to select an item or confirm a choice.
options.looks: Rounded square that fills with accent and shows a checkmark.
options.motion: Box fills from center (scale 0 to 1, 120 ms) and the checkmark draws on as a stroke (stroke-dashoffset, 150-200 ms); list item may strike through or dim.
options.use: Task lists, forms, onboarding checklists, multi-select.
options.vs: Radio buttons are mutually exclusive; checkboxes are independent. Success state is a larger system confirmation.
options.prompt: Check the box by scaling an accent fill from 0 to 1 inside the 18-20px rounded square (4-5px radius) over 120 ms, then draw a 2px white checkmark with stroke-dashoffset over 180 ms power2.out; for task items, draw a strikethrough across the label and dim it to 50% over 250 ms.

options.what: Mutually exclusive choice control where selecting one deselects the others.
options.looks: Circles with an inner filled dot on the selected option; often styled as selectable cards.
options.motion: Inner dot scales from 0 to 1 on the new choice while the old dot shrinks away (150-200 ms); selection cards move the highlight border between options.
options.use: Plan selection, settings, onboarding choices.
options.vs: Checkboxes allow many; radios allow one. Segmented controls and tabs are visually similar exclusive selectors.
options.prompt: Select the new option by scaling its 8px inner dot from 0 to 1 with back.out(1.5) over 180 ms while the previous dot scales to 0 in 120 ms; for card-style radios, move a 2px accent border to the chosen card and tint it 6% accent.

options.what: A button that opens a list of options below it.
options.looks: Trigger with a chevron; a floating menu panel with rows, hover highlight and check on the selected item.
options.motion: Chevron rotates 180 degrees; menu scales from 0.96 and fades in, origin top, 150-200 ms; items may stagger 15-25 ms; on choice, menu closes and the trigger label swaps.
options.use: Forms, filters, settings, any choice demo.
options.vs: Context menu opens at the pointer on right-click; dropdown opens from a trigger. Popover can hold any content, dropdown holds options.
options.prompt: Rotate the chevron 180 degrees in 150 ms; open the menu with transform-origin at the top, scale 0.96 to 1 and opacity 0 to 1 over 160 ms power2.out, items staggering 20 ms; highlight the hovered row with a 6% tint; on selection, show a check, close in 120 ms and crossfade the trigger label.

options.what: A menu of actions appearing at the pointer on right-click or long press.
options.looks: Compact floating panel anchored at the cursor, with grouped actions, icons, shortcut hints, and dividers.
options.motion: Scales in from the cursor point (origin at the click) 0.95 to 1 in 120-160 ms; submenus slide out sideways.
options.use: Desktop and design tools, file managers, power-user features.
options.conveys: Depth of capability and pro-level control.
options.vs: Dropdown opens from a visible trigger; context menu appears wherever the user right-clicks.
options.prompt: Open the menu anchored at the cursor, transform-origin at the click point, scale 0.95 to 1 and opacity 0 to 1 over 140 ms; 28-32px rows with icons and right-aligned shortcut hints; highlight the hovered row with an accent pill, and open submenus with an 8px sideways slide in 120 ms.

options.what: Invoking a keyboard-launched search-and-command overlay and running an action from it.
options.looks: Centered overlay input with filtered action list and shortcut hints over a dimmed backdrop.
options.motion: Shortcut pressed, palette scales in 0.96 to 1 (150-180 ms), backdrop dims; query types; list filters live with items reordering (FLIP); highlight slides; Enter flashes the row and closes the palette as the action executes.
options.use: Keyboard-first productivity and developer tools.
options.vs: Command-palette UI (ui-treatment) is the palette as the visual subject; this option is the interaction sequence of invoking and using it. Search is broader content lookup.
options.prompt: Show the Cmd+K keycaps, then scale the palette from 0.96 to 1 with opacity over 160 ms while dimming the backdrop to 40%; type the query at 45 ms per character, filtering the list with FLIP reorders (200 ms); slide the highlight between rows in 100 ms; on Enter, flash the row 10% brighter, close the palette in 120 ms and run the action.

options.what: Entering a query and receiving matching results.
options.looks: Search field with magnifier icon, query text, results list or grid, highlighted matching characters.
options.motion: Field expands on focus (width grows 150-250 ms), query types, results enter with staggered fade and 6-8px rise, match highlights appear.
options.use: Content products, e-commerce, knowledge bases, internal tools.
options.conveys: Findability: whatever you need is right there.
options.vs: Autocomplete suggests completions while typing; search returns results. Command palette mixes search with actions.
options.prompt: Expand the search field on focus from icon or compact width to full width over 220 ms power2.out; type the query; show results entering with a 40 ms stagger (opacity 0 to 1, y 8px to 0, 250 ms) and highlight matching characters in bold or accent.

options.what: Suggestions appearing and updating as the user types, or ghost text completing the input.
options.looks: Suggestion list under the input with matched portion bold, or gray ghost text after the caret (as in AI code completion).
options.motion: List updates with each keystroke (items crossfade/reorder in 100-150 ms); ghost text fades in at 40% opacity; Tab accepts it and the ghost text solidifies in 100 ms.
options.use: Search, forms, code editors, AI writing tools.
options.vs: Search returns results after a query; autocomplete predicts during typing. Streaming text is output arriving; ghost text is a suggestion awaiting acceptance.
options.prompt: As the user types, update a suggestion list beneath the input with crossfades and FLIP reorders (120 ms), bolding the matched portion; for inline completion, fade gray ghost text (40% opacity) in after the caret over 150 ms, show a small 'Tab' keycap, and on accept solidify the text to full color in 100 ms.

options.what: A file or asset being sent into the product, from drop or selection to processed.
options.looks: File card or thumbnail, progress bar or ring, filename and size, then a completed or preview state.
options.motion: File drops in, a progress bar fills with non-linear pace (quick start, slower middle, quick finish) over 1-2 s, then morphs into a checkmark or the file's preview.
options.use: Storage, media, document and AI-input products.
options.conveys: Ease and reliability; your content is safely in.
options.vs: Drop is the gesture; upload is the transfer and processing. Progress is the generic indicator.
options.prompt: Show a file card (icon, filename, size) entering the drop zone, then a 4px progress bar filling with an uneven pace (0-60% in 400 ms, 60-90% in 600 ms, 90-100% in 200 ms); morph the bar into a green check over 250 ms and expand the card into a thumbnail preview.

options.what: Content being exported or saved out of the product.
options.looks: Download icon, arrow into tray, progress ring, file appearing in a downloads stack or dock.
options.motion: Arrow drops downward into a tray (200-300 ms), a ring fills, then a file icon arcs toward a downloads location and bounces lightly.
options.use: Export features, reports, media apps, installers.
options.vs: Upload moves content in; download moves it out. Success state confirms any completed action.
options.prompt: On click, animate the download arrow dropping 6px into its tray in 220 ms, then fill a 2px progress ring around the button over 800-1200 ms; on completion, morph to a check and fly a small file icon on a curved arc to the downloads location in 500 ms power2.inOut.

options.what: A determinate indicator showing how much of a task is complete.
options.looks: Bar, ring or step indicator with fill in accent and optional percentage label.
options.motion: Fill advances with eased, non-uniform steps (never constant linear), label counts up in sync, completion triggers a success transition.
options.use: Uploads, onboarding steps, processing, setup flows.
options.vs: Loading is indeterminate (unknown duration); progress is determinate. Stepper progress shows discrete stages.
options.prompt: Fill a 4-6px rounded progress bar (or 3px ring) in accent from 0 to 100% in 3-5 irregular eased steps totalling 1.5-2.5 s, a tabular-figure percentage counting in sync; at 100%, flash the fill 10% brighter and morph into a success check within 250 ms.

options.what: An indeterminate wait state: spinner, pulsing dots or skeleton shimmer.
options.looks: Rotating arc spinner, three pulsing dots, or skeleton blocks with a shimmer sweep.
options.motion: Spinner rotates at ~1 revolution per 0.8-1 s with the arc length breathing; dots pulse in sequence 150 ms apart; skeleton shimmer sweeps every 1.2-1.6 s; loaded content replaces placeholders with a crossfade.
options.use: Any network wait, AI thinking, data refresh.
options.conveys: Activity and responsiveness during a wait. In a video, keep it short: loading beats read as slowness.
options.vs: Progress is determinate; loading is indeterminate. Streaming text replaces loading in AI products by showing partial output.
options.prompt: Keep loading states under 1 s of screen time: rotate a 2px arc spinner (20px) at one revolution per 900 ms, its arc breathing between 60 and 270 degrees; or sweep a shimmer across skeleton blocks every 1.4 s; replace with real content by crossfading and staggering items 30-40 ms.

options.what: Visual confirmation that an action completed.
options.looks: Green check (drawn stroke inside a circle), button turning green with 'Done', optional confetti or particle burst.
options.motion: Button morphs to a circle (width collapses 250 ms), check draws on (200 ms), a pulse ring expands; returns to rest or advances the flow after a 600-1000 ms hold.
options.use: Checkout, forms, deploys, sending, any completed task.
options.vs: Checkbox is user selection; success is system confirmation. Toast can carry a success message but is a surface.
options.prompt: Morph the button into a 48px green (#22C55E) circle by collapsing its width over 250 ms power2.inOut, draw a 3px white check with stroke-dashoffset over 220 ms, then emit a single ring expanding to 1.6x and fading over 400 ms; hold 800 ms before the next beat. Confetti only for milestone moments.

options.what: Visual indication that an action failed or input is invalid.
options.looks: Red border and icon, inline error message below the field, error banner.
options.motion: Horizontal shake of the field (3-4 cycles, 6-8px amplitude, 300-400 ms total), border turns red in 120 ms, message slides down 4px and fades in.
options.use: Forms, validation, before-state in problem-solution stories.
options.conveys: Friction (or, followed by a fix, how the product prevents it).
options.vs: Error is system feedback on failure; the 'problem' beat of problem-solution may show broader pain beyond a single error.
options.prompt: On error, shake the field horizontally with damped oscillation (8px, -6px, 4px, -2px, 0 over 350 ms), switch its border to red (#EF4444) in 120 ms, and slide a 13px red error message down 4px with a fade over 180 ms below it.

options.what: An alert arriving from the system or app, usually at the top of the screen or in a bell badge.
options.looks: OS-style banner with app icon, title and body; or a red badge count on an icon.
options.motion: Banner slides down from above the top edge with a spring settle (350-450 ms), holds 1.5-2 s, slides up; badges pop in with scale 0 to 1.2 to 1 and count increments with a roll.
options.use: Mobile features, alerts, real-time collaboration, social proof moments.
options.vs: Toast is an in-app transient message usually at the bottom; notification is system-level or an alert center. Widget UI (ui-treatment) is the visual style.
options.prompt: Slide a notification banner (app icon, bold title, one-line body, 20px radius, glass or solid surface) down from -120px to 12px from the top over 400 ms with a gentle spring (back.out(1.2)); hold 1800 ms; exit upward in 250 ms power2.in. For badges, pop scale 0 to 1.2 to 1 over 250 ms and roll the count digit.

options.what: A small transient in-app message confirming an action, usually at the bottom or corner.
options.looks: Compact dark or neutral pill/card with icon, short message and optional Undo action.
options.motion: Slides up 16-24px and fades in (200-250 ms), holds 2-4 s (shorter in video: 1-1.5 s), exits downward or fades; multiple toasts stack with scale and offset.
options.use: Saves, copies, sends, undo patterns.
options.vs: 'Snackbar' is Material's term, 'toast' is general web usage. Notification is system-level and more prominent; modal blocks interaction.
options.prompt: Enter the toast at bottom center or bottom right: y 20px to 0 with opacity 0 to 1 over 220 ms power2.out; compact 44-52px tall pill with icon and message; hold 1200 ms in video; exit by fading and dropping 8px over 180 ms. Stack additional toasts behind at scale 0.95 and 8px offsets.

options.what: A focused dialog that overlays the interface and blocks interaction behind it.
options.looks: Centered card with title, content and actions over a dimmed or blurred backdrop.
options.motion: Backdrop fades to 40-60% dark (200 ms) or blurs; dialog scales 0.95 to 1 with fade (200-250 ms), or rises 16px; exits faster (150 ms).
options.use: Confirmations, forms, feature spotlights, onboarding steps.
options.vs: Drawer slides from an edge and keeps context; popover is anchored and non-blocking; modal is centered and blocking.
options.prompt: Dim the backdrop to 50% black (or blur 8px) over 200 ms; scale the dialog from 0.95 to 1 with opacity 0 to 1 over 220 ms power2.out, centered, 16-20px radius, layered shadow; close in 150 ms with the reverse, slightly faster.

options.what: A panel sliding in from a screen edge to show secondary content while keeping context.
options.looks: Full-height side panel or bottom sheet with grab handle, over a lightly dimmed background.
options.motion: Slides in from the edge over 300-400 ms with a decelerating ease (power3.out or gentle spring); bottom sheets can snap between detents; background may scale down 0.95 (iOS card style).
options.use: Detail views, settings, mobile actions, carts.
options.vs: 'Drawer' is web/Material usage, 'sheet' is Apple usage. Modal is centered and blocking; popover is anchored and small.
options.prompt: Slide the drawer in from the right edge (or a bottom sheet from below) over 350 ms power3.out, full height, 400-480px wide, with a subtle left-edge shadow; dim the background to 20%; for sheets, show a 36x5px grab handle and optionally scale the underlying page to 0.95 with a 12px radius.

options.what: A small floating panel anchored to a trigger, holding rich content or controls.
options.looks: Card with a pointer arrow or offset toward its trigger, containing a form, picker or details.
options.motion: Scales 0.96 to 1 from the side nearest the trigger (transform-origin at the anchor) over 150-200 ms; exit in 120 ms.
options.use: Date pickers, share menus, quick edits, profile cards.
options.vs: Tooltip is a tiny read-only label; dropdown lists options; popover holds richer interactive content.
options.prompt: Open the popover anchored 8px from its trigger with transform-origin on the trigger side: scale 0.96 to 1 and opacity 0 to 1 over 170 ms power2.out; 12px radius, layered shadow, optional 8px arrow; close in 120 ms.

options.what: A small label explaining an element on hover or focus.
options.looks: Tiny dark pill with 12px text, sometimes a shortcut hint, positioned above the element.
options.motion: Appears after a 300-500 ms hover delay (shorter in video: 150 ms) with fade and 4px slide from the element (120-150 ms); disappears immediately on leave.
options.use: Icon buttons, onboarding hints, pointing out features in a demo.
options.vs: Popover is interactive and larger; callout annotation (product-demo) is an editorial overlay outside the UI, while a tooltip is part of the UI.
options.prompt: After the cursor has rested 150 ms on the element, fade in a dark tooltip (#111 at 90%, 6px radius, 12px text, optional keycap hint) 8px above it with a 4px upward slide over 130 ms; remove it in 80 ms when the cursor leaves.

options.what: A card growing seamlessly into a full detail view, with its content morphing into place.
options.looks: A list or grid card that enlarges to fill the screen or a large panel; its image and title travel to new positions.
options.motion: FLIP/shared-element morph: the card's bounds interpolate to the detail view over 400-600 ms power3.inOut while its image and title move to their new positions; siblings fade or push away.
options.use: Galleries, app store style detail views, feature deep-dives, transitioning from overview to detail.
options.conveys: Continuity and spatial logic: the detail is inside the card.
options.vs: Modal appears over the page; card expansion transforms the card itself. Accordion expands inline and pushes content down.
options.prompt: Expand the clicked card into the detail view with a FLIP transition: interpolate its position, size and corner radius (e.g. 16px to 0) over 500 ms power3.inOut, move its image and title to their destination positions in the same timing, fade sibling cards to 0 and blur them 4px, then stagger the detail content in 40 ms apart.

options.what: Sections that expand and collapse inline to reveal content.
options.looks: Stacked rows with chevrons or plus icons; expanded row shows content below; others push down.
options.motion: Height animates from 0 to auto (250-350 ms power2.inOut), chevron rotates 90-180 degrees or plus turns to minus, content fades in slightly after height starts; siblings slide.
options.use: FAQs, settings, sidebars, step lists.
options.vs: Card expansion morphs into a new view; accordion expands in place. Drawer overlays.
options.prompt: Expand the row by animating height from 0 to content height over 300 ms power2.inOut, rotating its chevron 180 degrees in sync; fade the content in from opacity 0 with a 4px rise starting 80 ms in; rows below slide down with the same curve; collapse the previously open row simultaneously.

options.what: Moving between sibling views via tabs or a segmented control.
options.looks: Tab bar with an active indicator (underline or pill background) and content panel beneath.
options.motion: Indicator slides and resizes to the new tab (200-300 ms power2.inOut); content crossfades or slides horizontally in the direction of travel (20-40px).
options.use: Showing multiple features or views in one screen, settings, dashboards.
options.conveys: Breadth within one place; organised views.
options.vs: Page navigation changes the whole page; tab switching swaps a panel within the page.
options.prompt: Slide the active tab indicator (2px underline or pill background) to the new tab, animating x and width together over 250 ms power2.inOut; crossfade content while sliding it 24px in the direction of travel (outgoing 150 ms, incoming 250 ms starting 50 ms later).

options.what: Moving from one full screen or page to another within the product.
options.looks: Current page exits and new page enters; nav item highlights; breadcrumbs update.
options.motion: Platform-typical transitions: push (new page slides in from right, old shifts left 30% and dims, 350-450 ms), fade-through (out 100 ms, in 200 ms), or shared-axis slides; sidebar highlight moves.
options.use: Walkthroughs across multiple screens, app demos, onboarding flows.
options.conveys: Flow and structure; the product is coherent.
options.vs: Tab switching swaps a panel; page navigation swaps the whole screen. Transitions dimension governs cuts between video scenes, not in-app routes.
options.prompt: Navigate by pushing the new page in from the right (x 100% to 0, 400 ms power3.out) while the old page shifts to x -30% and dims to 80%; move the sidebar's active highlight to the new item in 250 ms; for web products use a fade-through (old out 100 ms, new in 200 ms with 8px rise).

options.what: Dragging a list down past its top to reload content.
options.looks: List stretches down revealing a spinner or custom indicator above; new items appear at top.
options.motion: List tracks the finger with resistance (moves ~50% of finger distance), indicator rotates in proportion, releases into a spinner, then content snaps back and new rows slide in.
options.use: Mobile feeds, inboxes, social apps.
options.vs: Scroll moves through existing content; pull to refresh fetches new content.
options.prompt: Drag the list down 80-100px with rubber-band resistance (content moves half the finger distance), rotating a refresh indicator in proportion; on release, spin it for 600-800 ms, then snap the list back up in 300 ms power2.out and slide 1-3 new rows in from the top with a 50 ms stagger.

options.what: The user speaking to the product, visualized as audio activity and transcription.
options.looks: Microphone button, waveform bars or pulsing orb reacting to speech, live transcript text.
options.motion: Mic button pulses with an expanding ring; 5-30 waveform bars animate in amplitude (driven by the audio if present); transcript words appear as recognized, slightly behind the voice.
options.use: Voice assistants, AI products, dictation, accessibility features.
options.vs: Typing is keyboard text entry; streaming text is system output. Audio-reactive visuals (sound dimension) are decorative, voice input is functional UI.
options.prompt: On tap, pulse the mic button with a ring expanding to 1.8x and fading every 900 ms; show 12-24 rounded waveform bars (3-4px wide) whose heights follow the voice amplitude (or a smoothed random 20-100% pattern at 60-100 ms updates); reveal transcript words 150-250 ms after they are spoken, each fading in from 40% to 100%.

options.what: Visualizing data leaving the client for a server or service.
options.looks: Code snippet or request panel (method, endpoint, JSON body), connector line from client to server node, packet dots travelling.
options.motion: Request code types or highlights; a packet dot or light pulse travels along a connector path (300-600 ms); server node pulses on receipt; status chip shows 'pending'.
options.use: Developer platforms, APIs, infrastructure, integrations.
options.conveys: Technical clarity, speed, systems working together.
options.vs: Response is the return trip with data; API request is the outbound call. Workflow visualization (product-demo) shows whole processes.
options.prompt: Show a request panel (e.g. POST /v1/charges with a short JSON body in monospace syntax colors); highlight it, then send a 6-8px glowing dot along a bezier connector from client to server node over 450 ms power2.inOut; pulse the server node (scale 1.06, glow) on arrival and show a 'pending' chip with a spinner.

options.what: Data returning from a service and populating the interface.
options.looks: JSON response panel with status code (200 OK in green), latency label, UI elements filling with returned data.
options.motion: Return packet travels back; status chip flips to '200' with a color change; JSON lines reveal top to bottom (20-30 ms per line) and the UI fields populate with the values.
options.use: Developer products, integrations, AI tools, speed claims.
options.vs: Streaming text returns progressively as tokens; response returns as a payload. Success state confirms a user action.
options.prompt: Return a dot along the connector to the client in 350 ms, flip the status chip to '200 OK' in green with a latency label (e.g. '84 ms'), reveal JSON response lines top to bottom at 25 ms per line, then populate the corresponding UI fields with those values using quick 150 ms crossfades.

options.what: System-generated text appearing progressively, word or token at a time, as an AI produces it.
options.looks: Response block growing line by line, often with a soft cursor or fading leading edge; markdown formatting (bold, lists, code) resolving as it arrives.
options.motion: Chunks of 1-4 words arrive every 30-80 ms with slight irregularity; newly arrived words fade from 0-40% to 100% over 150-250 ms; container height grows smoothly; the view auto-scrolls.
options.use: AI assistants, copilots, chat products, generative writing tools.
options.vs: Typing is user input at human rhythm; streaming text is machine output in bursty chunks. A typewriter effect (letter by letter, constant rate) is a stylization, not how LLM output streams.
options.prompt: Stream the response in chunks of 1-4 words every 40-70 ms with irregular timing, each chunk fading from 30% to 100% opacity (and 2px blur to 0) over 200 ms; grow the container height smoothly (150 ms) and auto-scroll to keep the leading edge visible; render markdown styles as they complete.

options.what: The moment an AI creates an image, design, code or object from a prompt, including the thinking state and reveal.
options.looks: Shimmering or gradient-glow placeholder, 'thinking' indicator, progressive image resolve (noise to sharp), or layout elements materializing.
options.motion: Prompt submits; an animated gradient border or shimmer indicates thinking (1-2 s max in video); output resolves progressively (diffusion-style noise to sharp, blur to sharp, or elements assembling with stagger); a subtle sparkle or glow marks completion.
options.use: Generative AI products, AI features in existing tools, launch films for AI capabilities.
options.conveys: Creation, magic, intelligence. Overuse of sparkles and purple gradients now reads as generic.
options.vs: Streaming text is text-specific; AI generation covers any output. Loading is a neutral wait; generation shows the output forming.
options.prompt: After the prompt submits, rotate a conic-gradient border around the output container (one revolution per 2 s) for at most 1.5 s, then resolve the output progressively: images from heavy blur (24px) and noise to sharp over 1.2 s, or layout elements assembling with 40-60 ms stagger; finish with a single soft glow pulse, no confetti.

options.what: An AI agent's multi-step work shown as a live list of actions (searching, reading, editing, running).
options.looks: Vertical list of step rows with icons, spinners that become checks, short labels ('Reading 12 files', 'Running tests'), collapsible details.
options.motion: Each step row enters with a spinner, resolves to a check (200 ms) after 400-900 ms, and the next step appears beneath; completed steps compress or dim; final output reveals at the end.
options.use: AI agents, copilots, automation products, developer tools.
options.conveys: Autonomy and transparency: the agent is doing real work.
options.vs: Progress is one bar; agent steps are a narrated sequence of discrete actions. Step-by-step (product-demo) is an editorial structure; this is UI behavior.
options.prompt: Show a vertical list of agent steps: each row enters with opacity and 6px rise (200 ms) showing a 14px spinner and a short present-tense label; after 400-900 ms swap the spinner for a check (150 ms) and switch the label to past tense, dimming it to 60%; start the next row 100 ms later; finish by revealing the final output card.
